factual_claims.claim: Loan quality remained strong overall, but the prolonged Estonian recession led to higher overdue and forborne exposures, more restrictive consumer-finance lending, increased impairment allowances, and a rise in Stage 2 and Stage 3 loans.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Management Report states: 'The quality of the loan portfolio stayed strong, with some individual customers showing signs of weakening... During the full year LHV faced with healthy competition for deposits among banks... During the last couple of years, assets have been the limiting factor for growth, but this year the liabilities were... The Group fulfilled all the financial ratios... Estonian Corporate banking showed a strong growth... The quality of the loan portfolio remained strong, with a very low share of non-performing loans... Credit losses increased by EUR 4.4 million... The quality of the loan portfolio remained strong, with a very low share of non-performing loans... Expected credit losses on financial assets measured at amortised cost increased to EUR 16.3 million (2023: EUR 11.5 million)... The Group's cost to income ratio was a decent 43.4%... A decrease of the Group’s cost to income ratio to that level would increase the net profit by 19%... By the end of December, the total volume of the Group’s net loan portfolio amounted to EUR 4.6 billion (2023: EUR 3.6 billion), an increase of 28%. The portfolio could be divided to three: Estonian corporate banking loans increased by 21% to EUR 2.3 billion (2023: EUR 2.0 billion). Estonian retail loans increased by similar 21%, amounting to EUR 1.9 billion (2023: EUR 1.6 billion). Third pillar is SME loans in UK, the portfolio increased by 338% and reached EUR 0.3 billion... The volume of deposits increased by 21% and totalled EUR 6.9 billion by the year-end (2023: EUR 5.7 billion)... The share of demand deposits decreased to 64% (2023: 66%), as interest rates increased and made term deposits more attractive to customers... LHV Pank reduced deposits collected from deposit platforms by 1/3 and will continue to decrease them... Overdue loans remained at historically low levels throughout 2024, though there was a slight increase during the year. By year-end, the market average share of loans overdue by more than 60 days stood at 0.3%, reflecting continued stability in the credit market.'

candidate_sentences.text: Loan quality remained strong overall, but the prolonged Estonian recession led to higher overdue and forborne exposures, more restrictive consumer-finance lending, increased impairment allowances, and a rise in Stage 2 and Stage 3 loans.

candidate_sentences.text: The share price fell 7% to EUR 3.245.

verified_key_information_units.information: Consolidated revenue increased by 11% to EUR 338.3 million in 2024, driven by net interest income growth of 8% to EUR 273.3 million and net fee and commission income growth of 24% to EUR 60.3 million; net profit rose 7% to EUR 150.3 million, resulting in a cost-to-income ratio of 43.4% and return on equity of 24.5%.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report, Summary of the year 2024 (pages 10-11); Consolidated statement of profit or loss (page 189)

candidate_sentences.text: Net income increased 11% to EUR 338.3 million, supported by 8% growth in net interest income to EUR 273.3 million and a 24% increase in net fee and commission income to EUR 60.3 million.
Nevertheless, the cost-to-income ratio remained 43.4%, and return on equity was 24.5%, compared with 29.0% in 2023.

verified_key_information_units.information: The loan portfolio expanded by EUR 990 million (28% YoY) to EUR 4.6 billion, comprising Estonian corporate loans up 21% to EUR 2.3 billion, Estonian retail loans up 21% to EUR 1.9 billion, and UK SME loans up 338% to EUR 0.3 billion.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report, Summary of the year 2024 (page 10); Note 12, Loans and advances to customers (page 223)

candidate_sentences.text: Total assets increased 23% to EUR 8.7 billion, net loans rose 28% to EUR 4.6 billion, and customer deposits increased 21% to EUR 6.9 billion.
Loan growth reflected 21% increases in both Estonian corporate and retail lending, while UK SME loans expanded 338% to EUR 348 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Deposits grew by EUR 1,179 million (21% YoY) to EUR 6.9 billion, with regular customer deposits in LHV Pank rising EUR 554 million (14% YoY to EUR 4.6 billion) and deposits from financial intermediaries increasing significantly (LHV Bank collections up EUR 416 million, +388% YoY), partly offset by LHV Pank reducing platform deposits by one-third.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report, Summary of the year 2024 (page 10); Note 17, Deposits from customers (page 226)

candidate_sentences.text: Total assets increased 23% to EUR 8.7 billion, net loans rose 28% to EUR 4.6 billion, and customer deposits increased 21% to EUR 6.9 billion.
Deposit growth was supported particularly by term deposits, although LHV Pank reduced platform deposits by one-third.

verified_key_information_units.information: Assets under management increased to EUR 1.56 billion (3% YoY), primarily due to positive market returns, with LHV Varahaldus maintaining a ~25% market share in Estonia's II pillar pension system managing savings for 22.3% of participants.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report, Summary of the year 2024 (page 10); Overview of LHV Varahaldus (page 24)

verified_key_information_units.information: Customer base grew with LHV Pank reaching 456,000 clients (+9% YoY, including 38,000 new customers), and LHV Kindlustus insuring 170,000 customers (+6% YoY).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report, Summary of the year 2024 (page 10); Overview of LHV Kindlustus (page 24)

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic initiatives included launching retail banking operations in the UK, introducing a mobile banking app, and implementing cost-control measures involving redundancies and departmental restructuring to enhance operational efficiency.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Letter from the CEO (page 8); Overview of LHV Bank Ltd (page 25); Management report, Development activities (page 22)

verified_key_information_units.information: The dividend proposal recommends paying EUR 0.09 per share (total EUR 29.2 million) with related income tax of EUR 8.2 million, and transferring EUR 123.2 million of parent-company attributable profit to retained earnings.

The Group maintained strong regulatory capital positions with a CET1 ratio of 16.89% (above minimum 12.41%), complying with all capital adequacy (including MREL of 33.24% and 12.41%), leverage ratio (6.71%), and liquidity requirements (LCR 187.5%, NSFR 154.4%).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Regulatory and financial ratios (page 13); Note 21, Shareholders' equity (page 230)

candidate_sentences.text: Capital and liquidity remained strong.
The total capital adequacy ratio was 20.68%, down from 23.45%, while CET1 was 16.89%.
LCR and NSFR were 187.5% and 154.4%, respectively, both well above regulatory minima.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operations occurred amid a contracting Estonian economy (GDP -0.7% YoY) and stabilized UK economy, with LHV Pank maintaining tight credit quality (loans overdue >60 days at 0.3% of portfolio) and benefiting from rising corporate loan demand late in the year.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Business environment (page 18); Market average share of overdue loans (page 20); Overview of LHV Pank (page 21)

candidate_sentences.text: AS LHV Group delivered record financial results in 2024 despite falling interest rates, severe competition for deposits and lending, increased regulation, and continued economic contraction in Estonia.

Loan quality remained strong overall, but the prolonged Estonian recession led to higher overdue and forborne exposures, more restrictive consumer-finance lending, increased impairment allowances, and a rise in Stage 2 and Stage 3 loans.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K8, and K9 are fully present with supporting sentences identified. K4 (Assets under management) and K5 (Customer base growth) are missing entirely. K6 (Strategic initiatives) and K7 (Dividend proposal) are also missing entirely. While HIGH criteria are mostly covered, the absence of multiple MEDIUM and HIGH items (K4-K7) prevents a higher score. The main financial picture is captured, but important omissions remain.

coherence_issues.description: Sentence S4 states profit before tax was EUR 175.1 million, but there is no explicit logical connection or explanation provided in the summary explaining how this figure relates to or derives from the previously mentioned consolidated net profit (EUR 150.3 million) and other income/expense components. The relationship between these key profitability metrics is left unexplained, creating a logical gap.

candidate_sentences.text: Profit before tax was EUR 175.1 million.
Consolidated net profit rose 7% to EUR 150.3 million, while profit attributable to the parent’s owners reached EUR 149.0 million.

details.coherence_justification: The summary is generally coherent with a clear narrative structure covering performance highlights, segment results, balance sheet growth, and outlook. Most statements logically follow from one another. The primary issue is the unexplained relationship between profit before tax (S4) and consolidated net profit (S2), creating a logical gap. There are no self-contradictions, severe organizational problems, or significant repetitions. Balance sheet figures (e.g., loans, deposits) show growth percentages that are internally consistent and do not constitute contradictions because the summary does not claim they are exhaustive additive components of a single total.
